### Organize personal Notes into standalone and project folders

```yaml

status: Pending
parent_pending_ids: []

relation: main

```

Description:
- Add named thematic folders for personal Notes both outside any project and inside an exact Companion project. Each folder contains separate notes rather than a combined document. Example: an Altai trip project contains Interesting places and Hotels folders; each hotel note retains descriptions, reviews, host names and other details, and each place note retains attractions, activities and food information. Standalone folders must support the same thematic organization without creating a project.

Expected behavior:
- Users can create and rename folders, browse a folder, create notes in a folder and move existing notes into or out of folders. Project views expose project-scoped folders and contained notes; the general Notes view supports standalone folders and notes without a folder. Preserve exact note content, IDs, retained history and existing project associations. Provide reviewed MCP read/preview/accept/original-receipt workflows for the intended agent folder operations under existing Notes consent and ownership boundaries, without implicit task or Habitica effects.

Current context:
- The current Notes model supports one optional versioned project association but no folder entity. Existing Ready task T-a48aa46e-fd3c-43ff-b9b3-3becddb47599 covers Notes/project UI and excludes additional persistence schema. Folder work is distinct; Process Pending must coordinate overlap and research folder nesting, membership cardinality, cross-project moves, deletion behavior, source isolation, migration and validation before defining implementation units. No task dependency is asserted during intake.

Source:
- Direct repository-owner request in the current conversation on 2026-10-29, following the Montenegro thematic-notes example and the Altai trip project/folders example. Scope is Pending intake through skill-tree-add-pending-task; implementation and promotion are deferred.
title: Organize personal Notes into standalone and project folders
